text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The edit preserves all existing content of notifications/sms.py (docstring, constants, TEMPLATES, render, sent_messages, delivery_status, queue_sms) unchanged and only adds MOVED_TEMPLATE and notify_rerouted. notify_rerouted correctly uses load_households(active_only=True) (verified in registry/register.py), filters households whose site is in the given sites and whose sms_ok is True (Household has both fields, per core/models.py), and calls the existing queue_sms with the approved 'DELIVERY_MOVED' template (present in TEMPLATES) and params {\"site\": h.site, \"day\": day}, matching the ticket's requirement for the approved moved-delivery message with the household's site and new day. It does not mint SMS ids itself — queue_sms assigns them — and lets queue_sms's errors propagate. Each household appears once in the registry and set(sites) deduplicates the input, so each affected household gets exactly one text. The function returns the list of queued SmsMessage objects as required."}}
reasoning:
The proposed edit keeps all existing functions unchanged (render, sent_messages, delivery_status, queue_sms, TEMPLATES, constants) and adds MOVED_TEMPLATE = "DELIVERY_MOVED" plus notify_rerouted. notify_rerouted loads active households, filters site in sites and sms_ok True, calls queue_sms with DELIVERY_MOVED template and params {"site": h.site, "day": day}. queue_sms itself re-checks sms_ok and raises if not agreed — but the filter already excludes those, so no error. Template exists in TEMPLATES. load_households(active_only=True) exists. Household has site and sms_ok fields. Returns list of messages. All correct.

One subtlety: "every affected household gets exactly one text" — if sites contains duplicates, set(sites) handles that; each household appears once in registry, so one text each. Fine.

Accept.
